You have enabled IEEE 80211 FT in your WLAN infrastructure. You want to verify roaming between APs (two at a time) and determine If all of your end-points are capable of performing fast roaming What tool would you use to achieve this goal?
RF Spectrum Analyzer and two spectrum adapters (one for each band)
Predictive design tool and two Wi-Fi adapters (one for each band)
Protocol Analyzer and two Wi-Fi adapters (one for each channel of the chosen bands)
WLAN scannerdiscovery tool and two WI-FI adapters (one for each channel of the chosen bands
C

Capture the old and new AP channels with a protocol analyzer while the client roams. The Reassociation Request and Reassociation Response frames show the client moving to the target AP; two adapters allow both channels to be monitored.
What should you do during the design process of a point to point bridge link to minimize CCI and ACl?
Choose a channel on the 5 GHz band outside of the UNII-1 and UNII-3 channels
Choose a channel on the 2.4 GHz band other than the over used 1. 6 and 11
Install the antennas and choose the least busy channel using trial and error problem solving
Perform an outdoor site survey in the area of both buildings and determine the best channel to use
D
A site survey at both bridge endpoints reveals local channel occupancy and interference, allowing the designer to choose a channel that works at both ends.

When creating a long-distance bridge link, it is important to know the channels in use by other networks on both ends of the link and within a reasonable range It is not as Important to know the channels in use in the middle area of the link. Why is this the case?
Interference happens at the receiver
interference happens at the transmitter
The signals in the middle of the link will increase the amplitude of your signal as it passes through them
Your RF LoS will always be far above any interference in the middle because the signal travels up and then back down to the remote 802.11 receiver
D

The main interference concern is often at the endpoints, where the receiver's signal level is lower relative to nearby WLANs. A clear Fresnel zone and high path clearance help protect the link, but the source's wording should be read carefully.
What is the purpose of a Physical Installation Guide document?
To inform the Install technicians of WLAN frame exchanges and communication methods
To provide clear instructions on the locations and mounting methods, and possible configuration steps for APs
To provide sources for purchasing the equipment needed to implement the WLAN
To prove that the WLAN meets the organization's requirements
B
A physical installation guide converts the RF design into field instructions: exact AP locations, mounting orientation and hardware, cabling expectations, and any required configuration steps.
What single tool, by design can be used to verify channel selection, encryption in use and number of APs above a specified signal threshold in a given location during deployment?
Spectrum analyzer
Spreadsheet
WLAN scanner
Throughput tester
C
A WLAN scanner passively discovers nearby APs and reports attributes such as SSID, BSSID, channel, security, and received signal level.
Before connecting, mounting and powering 213 total controller-based APs what action should be taken to ensure that they are configured by the controller once powered on and connected lo the network''
Configure profiles in the controller and assign them to the APs
Configure the controller to provide PoE to the APs
Configure the network to allow the APs to have direct Internet access immediately
Ensure mat TLS tunnels will work between the APs and the controller
A
Preconfiguring AP profiles and assigning them to APs in the controller ensures that newly connected APs receive the intended WLAN, radio, and policy configuration.

You have designed a WLAN with a plan for 87 APs m a large office building. The customer has informed you that the budget is not as large as they hoped and they can only purchase 53 APs What action should be taken?
Simply increase the output power of the APs by 30 percent to accommodate tor the smaller number of purchased APs
Perform a complete redesign of the wireless network and inform the customer if some original requirements cannot be accomplished
Remove as many walls as possible within the facility so that the signals can travel a g<eater distance
Use only 2.4 GHz radios because the signals can be received at a greater distance
B
When user density exceeds the original design assumptions, redesign capacity for the actual client count and application demand rather than simply turning up AP power.

During the deployment of a WLAN the customer complains that the chosen locations for several APs are ruining the aesthetics of the building Instead of changing AP locations and requiring a redesign, what action can you recommend1?
Cover the APs with any kind of decorative covering that makes them look better
Move the APs and then use the WLAN in whatever way it functions afterward
Tell the customer to hire someone else because you are a professional WLAN designer and aesthetics are not important to you
Purchase skins or covers designed for the APs so that they do not stand out and they match more closely the aesthetics of the environment
D
A purpose-designed nonmetallic cover can improve appearance while avoiding the severe RF attenuation caused by metal enclosures; manufacturer guidance and warranty terms still apply.

Install technicians are deploying a multi-floor WLAN that you have designed They have finished the first floor and all APs on that floor are powered on and functioning No APs on any other floors have been deployed at this time You are considering performing a post-deployment site survey of the first floor immediately to validate proper implementation What statement is true about this site survey if you perform it?
It will miss any impact on the WLAN caused by APs on other floors
It will show you how the first floor will function after all other floors are deployed
It will not work because the controllers cannot function properly until all APs licensed lo the controller are operational
It will result in a complete set of data informing you how clients will function after the entire WLAN is implemented
A
Validating one floor while APs on other floors are powered off misses vertical RF interactions, including co-channel interference from APs above and below.

During a validation site survey, you realize that the installers mounted some of the APs on the wall when the design called Tor a ceiling mount. They said that this was done because the cabling company did not have the right tools to run the cables above the ceiling. You know that this will cause a difference in how the Wi-Fi signal will radiate throughout the environment. What should you do in this case?
Leave it as it is because it will not have a significant impact
Blame the cabling company it the Wi-Fi doesn't work since they didnot do their job correctly
Turn up the power on the APs to accommodate for the difference
Advise the stakeholder that requirements will not be met and a new design process will be needed to meet the requirements
D

Mounting APs on a wall instead of the designed ceiling position changes antenna orientation and propagation. Notify the stakeholder that the requirements may not be met and redesign or reinstall correctly.
When performing a roaming test and packet capture at the same time, what are two particular frames that will be present when roaming between two APs is successful?
Beacon and DTIM
Probe Request and Probe Response
Association Request and Association Response
Reassociation Request and Reassociation Response
D
A successful roam to a new AP is confirmed by the reassociation exchange: the client sends a Reassociation Request and the target AP replies.
After successfully deploying and validating a WLAN infrastructure, who should be trained for a better understanding and management of the solution? (Choose the single best answer)
Support staff and end-users
CEOs and other executives
Guests and CEOs
WLAN designer and WLAN implemented
A
Support staff need operational knowledge to manage and troubleshoot the WLAN; end users need enough training to use the service effectively.
What happens when you double the channel width (for example, use channel bonding) in a BSS?
Higher noise and lower SNR at the receiver
Lower noise and higher SNR at the receiver
Lower noise and lower SNR at the receiver
Higher noise and higher SNR at the receiver
A
Doubling channel bandwidth doubles the integrated thermal noise power, adding about 3 dB of noise if the noise spectral density is unchanged. With the same received signal level, SNR decreases.
Which one of the following might be detected as a source of CCI during a post-validation survey in the 5 GHz band?
Other OFDM networks
Other ERP networks
Microwave ovens
Other HR/DSSS networks
A
Other OFDM WLANs using the same channel can contend for airtime and create co-channel interference in the 5 GHz band.
What is the primary reason for avoiding 160 MHz channels with 802.11 in the 5 GHz band'?
Only two or three 160 MHz channels exist in the current frequency allocation, in some regulatory domains only one exists
The data rate becomes too high which causes some clients to gain access to the medium and never let it go
The output power required for 160 MHz channels is more than most regulatory domains allow
No APs exist in production that can implement 160 MHz channels
A
160 MHz channels consume large contiguous blocks of 5 GHz spectrum, leaving very few independent channels for reuse. That increases co-channel contention and reduces channel-planning flexibility.
How can you increase efficiency in an 802.11n 2.4 GHz multiple-channel architecture network?
Disable 802.11b data rates
Use channels 1,3, 5, 7, 9, and 11
Use only channels 1 and 2
Use 40 MHz channels
A
Disabling 802.11b data rates removes legacy low-rate transmissions that consume disproportionate airtime, improving efficiency when no required clients depend on them.
What best describes ensuring coverage requirements in a deployed WLAN?
Measuring the signal strength and number of APs at each location and comparing it to the requirement specifications
Verifying that the WLAN can be seen from all required locations
Verifying that you can connect to the WLAN from all required locations with the least capable device
Verifying that a 3x3:3 gaming laptop can connect to the WLAN from all required locations
C
Coverage validation must use a representative least-capable client and confirm that required locations meet the defined connectivity threshold.

A WLAN that you designed has been deployed in one area, users are complaining that the network performs poorly. When you analyze the area you see that a new interferer has been introduced that was not there during the pre-design survey. You've been informed that the interferer cannot be removed as it is an essential IoT device. What action do you recommend?
Reconfigure the channel plan to work around the interferer
Increase the output power of the APs covering that area by at least 25 percent to overpower the interferer
Place a metal enclosure around the interferer
Use 40 MHz channels so that the devices can use either 20 MHz block depending on where the interferer operates
A
When a new interferer appears, identify its frequency and duty cycle, then adjust channel assignments or radio use to avoid the affected spectrum.

A designer has created a WLAN design that has been implemented in an organization. The network exists in a four-story building. Because each floor has an identical floor plan, the designer designed only one floor and had the installers duplicate the design on each floor. Now, in validation, it is not performing well. What best explains the problem caused by this process?

The result was that APs were above and below each other on the same channel, resulting in excessive CCI. The APs should have been deployed so that they were not directly above and below each other and so that they used varying channels between floors.
The result was that clients could only connect to APs on their floor and, in a multi-floor deployment, you want clients to connect to APs on other floors in case they roam between floors.
The result was that ACI was increased because the APs were deployed above and below each other on the same channels.
The result was that the frequency utilization was too low for the clients to capture RF waves on which to transmit their signals.
A
Identical floor plans do not mean identical RF conditions. Vertically aligned APs on the same channel can create strong co-channel interference between floors.

You are evaluating CCI impact in 2.4 GHz. During the post-validation survey, you determine that 2 or 3 APs are seen from every location in the 2.4 GHz band with signal strengths above -75 dBm from all seen APs. Does this show that CCI has been removed from the environment given that three nonoverlapping channels exist in 2.4 GHz and why?
Yes because you would see 3 APs in every location with a signal strength above -75 dBm if CCI exists
Yes, because the goal is to see only 1 AP at each location in 2.4 GHz
No, because CCI can exist even with signals as low as -85 dBm to -93 dBm
No, because the goal is to see only 1 AP at each location in 2.4 GHz
C

CCI can still occur when neighboring AP signals are weak, including around −85 to −93 dBm. The relevant question is whether same-channel energy is strong enough at the receiver to cause contention, not simply how many APs are visible.
